reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates that a Ti/Ni coating on diamond particles in an HEA matrix forms a beneficial interface, but it does not involve W–Cu composites, does not address thermal conductivity, and provides no data on irradiation effects. The key premises about specific intermetallic formation, void mitigation, and thermal conductivity improvement in W–Cu are unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Ti/Ni duplex coating can be applied to particles via magnetron sputtering
Coating promotes formation of intermetallic phases (Ni–W, Ti–Cu) that bridge W and Cu
Graded interlayer reduces interfacial energy and accommodates thermal expansion mismatch
Interlayer minimizes void formation and absorbs irradiation defects
Improved interfacial integrity leads to higher thermal conductivity
